content: Tentoxin is a naturally occurring cyclic tetrapeptide that is synthesized by phytopathogenic fungi belonging to the genus Alternaria, specifically Alternaria tenuis and Alternaria alternata. This compound has the unique ability to selectively induce chlorosis in various germinating seedling plants. Due to this property, tentoxin has been proposed as a potential natural herbicide for agricultural applications. The compound was first isolated and characterized in 1967 by George Templeton and his colleagues. Their findings were presented at the Mycotoxin Research Seminar held in Washington, D.C., on June 8–9, 1967, and were subsequently published by the United States Department of Agriculture.
